import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level for marker size to add another visual dimension
    sizes=(50, 400), # Define the range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.7, # Add transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    edgecolor='w', # Add a white edge to markers for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, and Stress Level', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Customize the legend for clarity
plt.legend(title='Stress Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Adjust plot limits for better data representation if needed (optional)

# plt.ylim(4, 10)

# Ensure the layout is tight to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
